researcher_notes: IDENTIFIED AND LOCATED: this is the authoritative national rule set that METU references and Sabancı restates. Published by YÖK's Eğitim-Öğretim Dairesi Başkanlığı at https://egitim.yok.gov.tr/tr/document/2969. KEY STRUCTURAL FINDING: it is published ANNUALLY and carries a cycle year - a 2026 edition sits alongside 2024 and 2025 editions of the companion 'Yurt Dışından Öğrenci Kabul Kriterleri'. So the shared national rule set is itself CYCLE-VERSIONED. 'One rule set, institutions linked to it' therefore needs a version dimension: an institution links to the 2026 Esaslar, not to a timeless YÖK rule.

researcher_notes: EXPLICIT TOOLING NEGATIVE, recorded so the next pass does not repeat these four dead ends. The Esaslar is a PDF and could not be read by this lane: (1) WebFetch returns the raw PDF, whose extraction step reports only binary/FlateDecode artifacts; (2) the host has no poppler (pdftotext/pdftoppm) and no pypdf/pymupdf, so neither the CLI nor the PDF-native reader works; (3) a hand-written zlib extractor recovered only embedded subset-font programs, not text, and a ToUnicode CMap decoder found zero cmap entries - consistent with a PDF 1.5+ file storing objects in compressed object streams; (4) opening the PDF URL in the browser caused the SITE to force a file-download dialog rather than rendering, so that route was abandoned and not retried. WHAT WOULD WORK: poppler installed on the host (brew install poppler), or any environment with pypdf/pymupdf. This is a HOST TOOLING GAP, not a site block and not an authority problem - the document is public and freely reachable at a .gov.tr URL that already passes the source-authority gate.

researcher_notes: A SECOND, SEPARATE annual national artifact: the international-student QUOTA guide, published with supporting tables (Tablo 3/4/5). Quotas and eligibility criteria are distinct documents on distinct schedules. Koç's page showing 2025 quotas while advertising Fall 2026 dates is explained by this - the quota artifact lags the criteria artifact, and an institution can legitimately be current on one and stale on the other.
